style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: An acrostic prayer of a man who is at once hunted, guilty, and teachable -- David threading the Hebrew alphabet through three needs he refuses to separate: rescue from enemies, pardon for sins, and instruction in the way. It opens with the whole self held up -- to You, O LORD, I lift my soul -- and its refrain is the waiting of hope: none who wait for You will be put to shame. The teaching-petitions come thick: show me Your ways, teach me Your paths, lead me in Your truth, for good and upright is the LORD, and therefore He instructs even sinners in the way and guides the humble in what is right. The confession is unsparing and twice-told -- remember not the sins of my youth; pardon my iniquity, for it is great -- and the pardon is asked for one reason only: for Your name's sake. Verse 14 is the psalm's hidden jewel: the secret counsel of the LORD, His intimate friendship, belongs to those who fear Him. The final verses return to the siege -- desolate, afflicted, enemies many and cruel -- and the prayer ends by widening from one man to a nation: redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

1.text: Of David. To You, O LORD, I lift up my whole soul.
1.amp: A Psalm of David. Unto You, O LORD [YHWH], do I lift up [nasa] my soul [nephesh].
1.notes: The Aleph line and the psalm's posture: nasa (H5375), the lifting-verb, applied to the nephesh (H5315) itself -- the whole inner man raised in open hands like an offering. Everything that follows is what a lifted soul says.

2.text: O my God, in You I have put my trust; do not let me be put to shame, and do not let my enemies exult over me.
2.amp: O my God [Elohim], I trust [batach -- lean my weight] in You: let me not be ashamed [bosh], let not mine enemies [oyeb] triumph [alats -- exult] over me.
2.notes: batach (H982), the leaning trust, presented as the ground of the plea: shame (bosh, H954) would fall on the God trusted as much as the man trusting. The oyeb's alats (H5970), the gloating dance, is what faith stakes its reputation against.

3.text: Indeed, none who wait for You will be put to shame; shamed will be those who deal treacherously without cause.
3.amp: Yea, let none that wait [qavah -- wait with taut hope] on You be ashamed [bosh]: let them be ashamed which transgress [bagad -- deal treacherously] without cause [reqam -- emptily].
3.notes: The principle behind verse 2: qavah (H6960), hope stretched like a cord, has never yet ended in bosh. The shame that exists is reassigned -- to the bogedim (H898), covenant-betrayers who break faith reqam (H7387), for nothing.

4.text: Show me the roads You walk, O LORD; train me in Your paths.
4.amp: Show [yada -- make known] me Your ways [derek], O LORD [YHWH]; teach [lamad] me Your paths [orach].
4.notes: The psalm's other engine, the disciple's request: derek and orach (H1870, H734), the road and the track worn into it -- and two teaching-verbs, yada and lamad (H3045, H3925). A hunted man asking for a syllabus is a man who knows where his real danger lies.

5.text: Set my feet walking in Your truth and instruct me, for You are the God who saves me; my hope waits on You the whole day through.
5.amp: Lead [darak -- make me tread] me in Your truth [emeth], and teach [lamad] me: for You are the God [Elohim] of my salvation [yesha]; on You do I wait [qavah] all the day [yom].
5.notes: darak (H1869): not only shown the path but walked on it -- guidance that moves the feet. The credential is Elohe yishi (H3468), God of my salvation, and the tempo is kol ha-yom: hope's waiting as an all-day occupation, not an emergency posture.

6.text: Remember, O LORD, Your deep compassions and Your covenant loves, for they have been from of old.
6.amp: Remember [zakar], O LORD [YHWH], Your tender mercies ['bowels', rachamim, the KJV margin -- womb-deep compassions] and Your lovingkindnesses [chesed -- covenant loves]; for they have been ever of old [olam].
6.notes: David asks God to zakar (H2142) two things about Himself -- rachamim (H7356), compassion from the womb, and chasadim, the plural chesed (H2617), covenant loves stacked across history. me-olam: mercy older than the sinner's record, the argument's whole leverage.

7.text: Do not remember the sins of my youth or my rebellions; according to Your covenant love remember me -- for the sake of Your goodness, O LORD.
7.amp: Remember [zakar] not the sins [chattath] of my youth [neurim], nor my transgressions [pesha]: according to Your mercy [chesed] remember [zakar] You me for Your goodness' [tuv] sake, O LORD [YHWH].
7.notes: Three zakar's in two verses arrange divine memory: remember Your mercy, forget my youth's chattath and pesha (H2403, H6588), remember ME -- but by the filter of chesed, le-maan tuvekha (H2898), for the sake of Your goodness. Selective memory asked of the only One entitled to it (cf. Jeremiah 31:34).

8.text: The LORD is good and straight-dealing; that is why He shows even sinners the road to walk.
8.amp: Good [tov] and upright [yashar] is the LORD [YHWH]: therefore will He teach [yarah -- instruct, aim] sinners [chatta] in the way [derek].
8.notes: The doctrine that makes verse 4 possible: God's tov and yashar (H2896, H3477) produce a 'therefore' aimed at chattaim (H2400) -- sinners get the instruction, not graduates. His uprightness does not exclude the crooked; it teaches them straight (cf. Luke 5:32).

9.text: He guides the humble in what is right, and He teaches the lowly His way.
9.amp: The meek [anav -- the humble, the lowly] will He guide [darak -- lead to tread] in judgment [mishpat -- what is just]: and the meek will He teach [lamad] His way [derek].
9.notes: Two enrollment criteria: sinners (v. 8) and anavim (H6035), the lowly -- the same word Jesus blesses in the Beatitudes' 'meek'. God's school has no admissions test except the absence of self-sufficiency; the darak and lamad of verse 5 are here promised, not merely asked.

10.text: All the paths of the LORD are covenant love and truth to those who keep His covenant and His testimonies.
10.amp: All the paths [orach] of the LORD [YHWH] are mercy [chesed] and truth [emeth] unto such as keep [natsar] His covenant [berith] and His testimonies [edah].
10.notes: kol orchot YHWH -- every track He leads on, without exception -- is paved with chesed and emeth (H2617, H571), the pair that is God's own name-gloss at Sinai. The perceiving condition: natsar (H5341) of berith and edot; covenant-keepers read the road's true material.

11.text: For the sake of Your name, O LORD, pardon my iniquity, great as it is.
11.amp: For Your name's [shem] sake, O LORD [YHWH], pardon [salach] mine iniquity [avon]; for it is great [rav].
11.notes: The center of the acrostic and one of Scripture's strangest arguments: forgive it BECAUSE it is rav (H7227), great -- a large pardon glorifies a large Name. salach (H5545), the God-only forgiveness-verb, requested le-maan shimkha: pardon as something God does for His own reputation (cf. Ezekiel 36:22).

12.text: Who is the man who fears the LORD? Him He will instruct in the way he should choose.
12.amp: What man [ish] is he that fears [yare] the LORD [YHWH]? him shall He teach [yarah] in the way [derek] that he shall choose [bachar].
12.notes: The third enrollment criterion: yirat YHWH. And the guidance promised respects human agency -- the derek 'that he shall bachar (H977)': God instructs the fearer in the choosing itself, so that the man's own decision lands on God's road.

13.text: His soul will lodge in goodness, and his descendants will inherit the land.
13.amp: His soul [nephesh] shall dwell ['lodge in goodness', lun be-tov, the KJV margin] at ease; and his seed [zera] shall inherit [yarash] the earth [eretz].
13.notes: lun be-tov: the God-fearer's nephesh spends its nights lodged in goodness -- security as sleeping arrangements. The zera inheriting eretz (H3423, H776) is the land-promise Jesus universalized: the meek shall inherit the earth (cf. Matthew 5:5; Psalm 37:11).

14.text: The intimate counsel of the LORD belongs to those who fear Him, and He makes His covenant known to them.
14.amp: The secret [sod -- the intimate council, the confidential circle] of the LORD [YHWH] is with them that fear [yare] Him; and He will show [yada -- make known] them His covenant ['and his covenant to make them know it', berith, the KJV margin].
14.notes: The psalm's hidden jewel: sod (H5475) is the council-circle where a king confides in his intimates -- Abraham's status when God would not hide Sodom's fate from him (cf. Genesis 18:17; Amos 3:7; John 15:15). Reverence is the entry badge to God's inner conversation.

15.text: My eyes are ever toward the LORD, for He will pull my feet free from the net.
15.amp: Mine eyes [ayin] are ever [tamid] toward the LORD [YHWH]; for He shall pluck ['bring forth', yatsa, the KJV margin] my feet [regel] out of the net [resheth].
15.notes: The posture of Psalm 123: eyes tamid on the Master, not on the trap. The resheth (H7568) is the fowler's mesh already around the feet -- and the psalmist watches God, not the knots, because yatsa (H3318), the bringing-out, is His work.

16.text: Turn Your face to me and be gracious to me, for I am alone and afflicted.
16.amp: Turn [panah] You unto me, and have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon me; for I am desolate [yachid -- alone, solitary] and afflicted [ani].
16.notes: yachid (H3173), the only-one word of Psalm 22:20 and Isaac's binding: solitary to the bone. panah and chanan (H6437, H2603) -- the turned face and the grace -- asked on the strength of need alone, which in this psalm has always been enough.

17.text: The troubles of my heart have grown wide; bring me out of my distresses.
17.amp: The troubles [tsarah] of my heart [lebab] are enlarged [rachab -- widened]: O bring You me out [yatsa] of my distresses [metsuqah -- the tight straits].
17.notes: A bitter reversal of the broad-place image: rachab (H7337), the widening that elsewhere means freedom, here describes the troubles themselves spreading. metsuqot (H4691) are the narrows; the prayer asks the yatsa of verse 15 for the whole heart, not just the feet.

18.text: Look upon my affliction and my toil, and lift away all my sins.
18.amp: Look [raah] upon mine affliction [oni] and my pain [amal -- toil, trouble]; and forgive [nasa -- lift off, carry away] all my sins [chattath].
18.notes: The three needs braided in one breath: oni and amal (H6040, H5999), the suffering -- and nasa (H5375), the same lifting-verb the psalm opened with, now asked of God: I lifted my soul to You (v. 1); You lift my sins from me. Every chattath, kol.

19.text: Look upon my enemies, for they are many, and they hate me with a violent hatred.
19.amp: Consider [raah] mine enemies [oyeb]; for they are many [rabab]; and they hate [sane] me with cruel ['hatred of violence', chamas, the KJV margin] hatred [sinah].
19.notes: A second raah: look at my sins (v. 18), now look at my enemies -- David hides neither column from the audit. sinat chamas (H8135, H2555), hatred with violence in it: not dislike but intent, and rabab, they multiply.

20.text: Guard my soul and rescue me; do not let me be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.
20.amp: O keep [shamar -- guard] my soul [nephesh], and deliver [natsal -- snatch away] me: let me not be ashamed [bosh]; for I put my trust [chasah -- take refuge] in You.
20.notes: The shame-plea of verse 2 returns with the refuge-verb chasah (H2620) as its warrant -- the psalm has traveled from batach, leaning, to chasah, sheltering. shamar the nephesh: the soul lifted in verse 1 is asked back into the Keeper's custody.

21.text: Let integrity and uprightness keep watch over me, for I wait for You.
21.amp: Let integrity [tom -- wholeness, blamelessness] and uprightness [yosher] preserve [natsar] me; for I wait [qavah] on You.
21.notes: tom and yosher (H8537, H3476) as bodyguards -- character itself posted as sentries. Not the merit that earns rescue but the integrity that hope produces; and the refrain returns to close the alphabet: qavah, I wait for You.

22.text: Ransom Israel, O God, from every one of his distresses.
22.amp: Redeem [padah -- ransom] Israel [Yisrael], O God [Elohim], out of all his troubles [tsarah].
22.notes: The line past the alphabet's end, like Psalm 34's: the acrostic finished, David adds one verse for everyone else. padah (H6299), ransom-redemption, for all Yisrael out of kol tsarot -- the private prayer refusing to stay private; a king's intercession as the last word.
